test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 16 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: P and Q together can complete a job in 20 days. Q and R together can complete the same job in 30 days. P and R together can complete the same job in 30 days. What is the respective ratio of the number of days taken by P when completing the same job alone to the number of days taken by R when completing the same job alone?
solution:
**Given:**

P and Q together can complete the job in 20 days.

Q and R together can complete the job in 30 days.

P and R together can complete the job in 30 days.

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

One-day work of P and Q = 1/20 ...........(1)

One-day work of R and Q = 1/30 ...........(2) 

One-day work of P and R = 1/30 ...........(3)

Adding the equations (1), (2), and (3)

(P + Q) + (R + Q) + (P + R) = (1/20) + (1/30) + (1/30)

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = (1/20) + 2(1/30)

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = (1/20) + (1/15)

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = (3 + 4)/60

⇒ (P + Q + R) = 7/120

Total work done by all P, Q, and R in one day is 7/120

Now total work done by P alone in one day

⇒ (P + Q + R) - (R + Q) = (7/120) - (1/30)

⇒ P = (7 - 4)/120

⇒ P = 3/120 = 1/40

P alone can do the job in 40 days

Now total work done by R alone in one day

⇒ (P + Q + R) - (P + Q) = (7/120) - (1/20)

⇒ R = (7 - 6)/120

⇒ R = 1/120 

R alone can do the job in 120 days

Now the ratio of work done by P and R alone

⇒ P/R = 40/120 = 1/3 = 1:3

**∴ The ratio of work done by P and R alone is 1:3.**
